To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

superparamagnetic composite particles based on CaCO3 /polymer/magnetite were obtained by mineralization of supersaturated solutions of CaCO3 in the presence of magnetite nanoparticles and polymer beads.
the presence of the magnetic nanoparticles in the composites allows the external manipulation and separation of the modified materials using a permanent magnet.
we developed a new method for the preparation of superparamagnetically modified ion exchangers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of superparamagnetic composite particles with different morphologies and with the evaluation of the influence of magnetite addition and the order of the addition on their sorption properties.
the synthesis of magnetic composites with a high content of magnetite, which is a prerequisite for magnetic separation.
the preparation and characterization of new superparamagnetic composite particles, which could be used in various fields such as catalysis, separation, and environmental protection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of magnetite particles in the ion exchangers does not affect the ion exchange process.
the composites prepared with magnetite and CIE beads showed higher sorption capacities for Cu2+ ions.

the composites prepared in the presence of the water-based magnetic fluid are characterized by a higher content of the CaCO3 phase, a higher thermal stability, and a higher capacity for CuII sorption, as compared to the samples prepared in the absence of magnetite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of magnetite to the polymer/CaCO3 composites increases the sorption capacity for metal ions.
the presence of magnetite in the composites does not affect their ion-exchange properties and that the composites can be easily separated and recycled using a permanent magnet.

the presence of magnetic nanoparticles in the ion exchangers provides a facile way of external manipulation using a magnetic field, thus allowing the magnetic separation and extraction of the magnetic modified material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition order of the magnetite and Ca2+ ions in the supersaturated solution is crucial to obtain a composite with a high sorption capacity for heavy metal ions.
the addition of magnetic nanoparticles to the polymer beads can be used for magnetic separation and recovery of the modified polymer.
the addition of magnetite nanoparticles in the preparation process of the ion-exchange resin composites leads to an enhancement in the ion-exchange capacity.
